content.overview: Section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 defines sale as a transfer of ownership in exchange for a price paid or promised or part-paid and part-promised. Transfer of tangible immovable property of the value of one hundred rupees and upwards can be made only by a registered instrument. An agreement to sell does not, of itself, create any interest in or charge on such property.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Transfer of ownership for price? (2) Immovable ≥ ₹100 — registered instrument? (3) Agreement to sell only — no interest? (4) Part-performance path under s. 53A?
content.study:
Title passes by the completed sale (registered deed where required), not by a mere agreement to sell. The buyer under an agreement may seek specific performance and, where ingredients are met, protection under s. 53A; that does not by itself confer ownership.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.body: Transfer of ownership for a price paid, promised, or part-paid and part-promised.

sections.heading: Formality
sections.body: Tangible immovable property of ₹100 and upwards — only by registered instrument.

sections.heading: Agreement to sell
sections.body: Creates no interest or charge in the property by itself.

sections.heading: Title passage
sections.body: Ownership passes under the completed sale, not under the bare agreement.

sections.heading: Link to s. 53A
sections.body: Part-performance may shield possession; it does not replace a completed sale as a source of title.

examples.title: Registered sale
examples.body: Vendor executes and registers a sale deed for land priced above ₹100 — ownership transfers under s. 54.

hypotheticals.question: Does an agreement to sell make the buyer the owner?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. s. 54 states that a contract for sale does not create any interest in or charge on the property.

distinctions.title: s. 54 sale vs s. 53A part-performance
distinctions.left: Transfer of ownership for price; registered instrument where required.
distinctions.right: Protective shield for possession under a written contract; does not confer title.

misconceptions.correction: s. 54: a contract for sale does not create any interest in or charge on such property.
